result:
The proposed answer, $\gamma = q/2$, is almost certainly wrong, because it drops the dependence on $\beta$ that the problem explicitly asks for.

The solution's main justification is that $\beta$ "is typically $d$" and can be ignored. That is an assumption the problem does not make. Ahlfors regularity of exponent $\beta$ allows $\beta < d$, since $\omega$ can concentrate on a lower-dimensional set. The energy distance with kernel $-|x-y|^q$ has Fourier decay $|\xi|^{-(d+q)}$, so its RKHS is a Sobolev-type space of order $q/2$. Approximation rates in such norms scale with the ratio of smoothness to the effective dimension of the measure. That effective dimension is $\beta$, which is why the rate should depend on $\beta$. A plausible form is $\gamma = \frac{q}{2\beta}$, possibly with an additional $\frac12$ term depending on normalization. Neither version reduces to $q/2$ for general $\beta$.

The solution also never derives or cites a rate result. It asserts $\gamma = q/2$ with no argument.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
